articles.headline: Reliance Industries eyes ₹1 trillion entry into aluminium business
articles.summary: Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries Ltd is evaluating a ₹1 trillion investment to enter the aluminium production sector. The move aims to leverage the company’s coal resources and diversify its metals portfolio. RIL recently won two coal blocks in Odisha and plans a coal gasification plant to convert coal into fuel for the energy-intensive aluminium smelting process.

articles.headline: Coal India to invest ₹1 trillion in rail and gasification projects
articles.summary: Coal India Ltd plans to invest ₹48,000 crore in rail connectivity and mechanized coal evacuation to reach a production goal of 1 billion tonnes by 2030. The firm is also committing ₹50,000 crore to joint-venture gasification projects with Bharat Heavy Electricals, GAIL, and IOCL. The move targets reducing logistics costs and diversifying into chemical manufacturing.

articles.headline: Trai proposes new 1600 series for bank and firm calls
articles.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) is discussing a dedicated 1600-number series for banks and financial institutions. The initiative aims to help consumers distinguish legitimate service-related calls from spam or fraudulent numbers. Industry executives noted that the series would allow callback functionality, improving trust and consumer convenience.

articles.headline: Naman Group wins bids for two luxury hotels for ₹1,800 crore
articles.summary: Mumbai-based Shree Naman Group has won a six-month bidding process to acquire the JW Marriott Hotel in Bengaluru and the Crowne Plaza in Pune for ₹1,800 crore. The properties were previously owned by the Advantage Raheja Group and were under insolvency proceedings. Naman Group plans to hold 100% ownership of both assets following the NCLT-approved resolution.

articles.headline: Sam Altman Swiss watch becomes the newest status symbol for OpenAI
articles.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and key staff are sporting a custom-designed Vanguard Swiss watch featuring the OpenAI logo. The 'Titanium Orb' watch, valued at roughly $180,000, was created for select company personnel. The timepiece includes intricate engravings like 'COMPUTE IS DESTINY' and 'SCALING,' reflecting Silicon Valley's obsession with AI advancement and exclusivity.

articles.headline: Piyush Goyal meets Japanese financial leaders to deepen investment ties
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal met with leaders of Japanese financial institutions in Tokyo to attract investments in green hydrogen, semiconductors, and digital infrastructure. Goyal highlighted India’s goal of becoming a $30-trillion economy by 2047. The discussions focused on leveraging Japan’s tech expertise and mobilizing long-term capital for India’s growth.

articles.headline: India issues new guidelines for multi-family organ swap transplants
articles.summary: The health ministry has introduced new protocols for organ swaps between families to address the shortage of donors. The system uses a national registry to match patients across the country, potentially facilitating 3,000 to 4,000 kidney transplants annually. The guidelines simplify legal approvals and aim to help the 200,000 patients currently awaiting transplants.

articles.headline: World Bank names India main driver of South Asia growth
articles.summary: A World Bank report identifies India as the primary growth driver in South Asia, with the region expanding faster than other developing economies. India's GDP growth is projected to outpace peers, though the report warns of risks from global supply chain shifts and the impact of AI on jobs. Regional trade remains low, with intra-regional trade accounting for only 5% of total trade.

articles.headline: India pivots to US for LPG and LNG as war disrupts Gulf
articles.summary: India has increased imports of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the US due to conflict in West Asia disrupting traditional Gulf supply routes. In February 2026, India imported roughly 0.62 million tonnes of LPG from the US, as domestic firms look to diversify energy sources and mitigate regional geopolitical risks.

articles.headline: Ribbit Capital to sell ₹1,914 crore stake in fintech Groww
articles.summary: Ribbit Capital is planning to sell shares worth up to ₹1,914 crore ($228 million) in Groww's parent company through a secondary block deal. The sale involves approximately 1.6% of Groww's existing shares at a floor price of ₹1,775 per share. Groww will not receive any proceeds from the transaction, which provides an exit for early investors.

articles.headline: VC firms flag UPI autopay data as new growth metric
articles.summary: Venture capital firms are shifting focus from surface-level UPI transaction volumes to 'autopay' data to identify active users. Concerns have risen over 'dead' users who have inactive mandates. Data shows top banks processed 1.8 billion UPI transactions in July, but VCs are now scrutinizing retention rates and actual user engagement to determine true platform value.

articles.headline: Drone startup Airbound raises $37 million in Series A funding
articles.summary: Bengaluru-based autonomous logistics startup Airbound has raised $37 million in a Series A round led by Lightspeed. The funding will be used to scale engineering, manufacturing, and go-to-market efforts for its deeptech drone technology. The firm aims to transform delivery logistics with high-efficiency drones that are significantly cheaper than traditional ground transport.

articles.headline: Vishal Mega Mart reappoints Gunender Kapoor as CEO for five years
articles.summary: The board of Vishal Mega Mart has reappointed Gunender Kapoor as managing director and CEO for another five-year term starting June 2027. The move aims to ensure leadership stability ahead of the company's anticipated IPO. Vishal Mega Mart reported a 19% year-on-year revenue growth in Q1 FY27, reaching ₹3,730 crore, supported by same-store sales growth.

articles.headline: Family offices increase participation in India's pre-IPO market
articles.summary: Ultra-high-net-worth individuals and family offices are increasingly investing in Indian startups and growth-stage companies before they go public. Assets under management for family offices in India have grown to over 300 from roughly 45 in 2018. This trend is driven by the desire for higher returns and a maturing private equity ecosystem as IPO listing gains become harder to achieve.

articles.headline: Hero MotoCorp revamps leadership to focus on electric vehicles
articles.summary: Hero MotoCorp has hired five senior leaders from outside the two-wheeler industry to steer its growth in electric vehicles and premium motorcycles. The new executives bring expertise from sectors like semiconductors and AI. This leadership overhaul, the largest since Pawan Munjal stepped down as CEO in 2023, reflects the company's strategy to diversify its product portfolio.

articles.headline: FedEx expands India investments as high-value exports surge
articles.summary: FedEx is increasing its investment in India following a 40% revenue growth in the country last year. The firm is focusing on high-value exports like electronics, engineering goods, and healthcare. New investments include a $100 million commitment to an air cargo hub at Navi Mumbai airport and a $250 million long-term investment in a hub at the Adani-operated Mumbai airport.

articles.headline: Kedaara Capital invests $200 million in Tynor Orthotics
articles.summary: Private equity firm Kedaara Capital has invested $200 million in Tynor Orthotics, a manufacturer of orthopaedic appliances. The deal valued the Mohali-based company at approximately ₹3,500-4,000 crore. Kedaara aims to help Tynor expand its international presence and R&D capabilities. Tynor currently has over 8,000 hospital partners and 300,000 retail outlets in India.

articles.headline: Indian IT firms pivot to client-asset acquisitions for growth
articles.summary: Major Indian IT companies like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro are increasingly acquiring the in-house IT assets and staff of their clients to secure long-term outsourcing deals. Recent examples include TCS’s deal with MHP and Wipro’s acquisition of Alight’s IT arm. This 'buy-to-grow' strategy provides immediate scale and deeper client relationships in a slowing global tech market.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping signals defiance as US warns of Iran sanctions
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping has expressed continued support for Iran despite US warnings of sanctions against Chinese entities for supporting Tehran's war economy. China remains Iran's largest oil buyer and a key economic lifeline. The US has threatened to target major Chinese banks if they do not reduce transactions with Iran, escalating trade tensions between the superpowers.

articles.headline: Canada retaliates with 50% tariffs on 700 US products
articles.summary: Canada will impose 50% tariffs on over 700 US goods, including steel, aluminium, and dairy, starting September 8. The move is a direct response to 50% import duties levied by the US on Canadian products earlier this year. Prime Minister Mark Carney accused the US of trying to 'destroy' Canadian industries, marking a sharp escalation in trade hostilities between the neighbors.

articles.headline: Avaada Electro plans $800 million IPO for solar manufacturing
articles.summary: Solar manufacturer Avaada Electro is planning an initial public offering (IPO) to raise as much as $800 million. The company has invited banks like ICICI Securities and JP Morgan for the mandate. Proceeds will be used to fund the expansion of its solar cell and module manufacturing capacity. The filing is expected by October 2025 with a target listing in early 2026.

articles.headline: Rivals challenge Nvidia's dominance in trillion-dollar AI chip market
articles.summary: Companies like Amazon, Google, and Meta are developing in-house AI chips to reduce dependence on Nvidia, which currently controls 90% of the market. Startups like Cerebras and Groq are also gaining ground with specialized architectures. While Nvidia’s GPUs remain the gold standard for training models, the industry is shifting toward more efficient chips for AI inference.

articles.headline: Airbnb rental premiums fade as hosts shift to longer stays
articles.summary: The premium earned by Airbnb hosts over conventional rentals is shrinking across major Indian cities due to an oversupply of short-term listings. In Tier-1 cities, the premium has fallen to 32.4%, while in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, it has dropped to 6.7%. Many hosts are now switching to monthly or long-term rentals to ensure more predictable and stable cash flows.

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies 1978 industry definition for labour disputes
articles.summary: A nine-judge bench of the Supreme Court has ruled that the 1978 definition of 'industry' from the Bangalore Water Supply case remains valid. This ensures that employees in hospitals, universities, and non-profits continue to be protected under the Industrial Disputes Act. The ruling clarifies the legal framework for millions of workers until new labour codes are fully implemented.

articles.headline: Amit Shah vows to remove all infiltrators from India
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated on Tuesday that India is not a 'dharamshala' and that illegal infiltrators who threaten national security and demographics will be removed. Speaking at a valedictory session of the Intelligence Bureau, he outlined a four-pronged border security strategy. Shah emphasized that the goal is to make India free of infiltrators in a very short period.

articles.headline: Cabinet approves extradition pacts with Kazakhstan, Kenya, and Kyrgyz Republic
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved extradition treaties with Kazakhstan, Kenya, and the Kyrgyz Republic. These pacts aim to provide a legal framework for the return of fugitive criminals involved in transnational crimes, terrorism, and drug trafficking. The move strengthens India's international cooperation in combating cross-border crime.

articles.headline: China defends Iran ties despite new US sanction threats
articles.summary: Beijing stated on Tuesday that it will not back down from its cooperation with Iran following new sanctions by the US targeting businesses in China and Hong Kong. Foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said China's cooperation with Iran is legitimate and should not be undermined. China remains Iran's largest trading partner, and its oil imports are a key part of the bilateral relationship.

articles.headline: BJP considers contesting all 117 Punjab assembly seats solo
articles.summary: Senior BJP leaders have indicated the party is prepared to contest all 117 seats in the 2027 Punjab assembly elections independently. While talks for an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) were previously explored, the party's national general secretary B.L. Santhosh stated that the doors remain open but the current strategy focuses on strengthening the party's solo presence.

articles.headline: Student protesters clash with police in Patna over recruitment
articles.summary: A protest by student organizations in Patna demanding a single test for teachers' recruitment turned violent as demonstrators clashed with police. Police used water cannons and batons to disperse the crowd after they broke through barricades while marching toward the chief minister's residence. Several protesters and police officers sustained injuries during the confrontation.

articles.headline: 81% of Bengal post-SIR pleas seek voter list deletions
articles.summary: Data reveals that nearly 3.11 million out of 3.84 million appeals filed before West Bengal’s appellate tribunals seek the deletion of names from electoral rolls. These appeals follow the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The Supreme Court noted that these cases must be prioritized as they affect voting rights and potential disenfranchisement of legitimate voters.

articles.headline: Kharge and Rahul urge PM to change census caste format
articles.summary: Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have asked the government to amend the format of the upcoming census to include a specific column for Other Backward Classes (OBCs). They argue that the current format, which only counts SCs and STs, hides the true demographic share of the OBC population. The leaders seek a comprehensive caste-based census for better policy planning.

articles.headline: Akal Takht slams fresh 21-day furlough for Ram Rahim
articles.summary: The Akal Takht has criticized the Haryana government's decision to grant a fresh 21-day furlough to Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh. Giani Kuldeep Singh Gurguj questioned why Singh is repeatedly granted parole while Sikh prisoners languish in jails despite completing their sentences. Singh is serving a 20-year sentence for rape and murder convictions.

articles.headline: Teen's body recovered from drain in Delhi after three-day search
articles.summary: The body of a 15-year-old boy, Mithun, was found in an open drain in Delhi's Jasola area three days after he fell into it. His parents had waited at the site through rain as search operations were conducted by the NDRF and local authorities. The family has blamed government apathy and uncovered drains for the tragedy, which sparked local protests over infrastructure safety.

articles.headline: Trump's proposed $103,265 H-1B fee threatens US credibility
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has proposed a massive $103,265 fee for H-1B visa applications, a move seen as a significant blow to the program. While the proposal is in a 30-day public comment period, it has sparked concerns about the US's economic competitiveness and its relationship with allies like India. The fee is significantly higher than the previous entry-level median wage for visa holders.

articles.headline: Centre notifies 'Keralam' as official name for Kerala state
articles.summary: The Union government has officially notified 'Keralam' as the new name for the state of Kerala, following a resolution passed by the state assembly. The Ministry of Home Affairs issued the notification under the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026. The move aligns the state's official name with its traditional Malayalam pronunciation.

articles.headline: Pakistan's Kirana Hills hit by 2025 munitions was unintentional: Ex-CDS
articles.summary: Former Chief of Defence Staff Gen Anil Chauhan stated that the striking of Pakistan's Kirana Hills in 2025 by Indian munitions was not a deliberate act. Speaking on the incident, he explained that the munitions were inadvertently launched during an event and landed near the nuclear facility site. The statement aims to clarify that there was no intent to target the strategic location.

articles.headline: SC stays FIR against journalist in alleged road rage case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has granted interim relief to a journalist by staying an FIR filed against him in an alleged road rage case in Uttar Pradesh. The journalist claimed the case was a retaliatory measure for his reporting on irregularities at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. The court has asked the state government to respond to the plea seeking the quashing of the charges.

articles.headline: Bombay HC to rehear Volkswagen challenge to $1.4bn tax
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court is set to rehear a challenge by Volkswagen against a $1.4 billion tax demand from Indian authorities. The case involves allegations that the carmaker evaded import duties by bringing in components as nearly complete units. A new bench will be constituted to hear the final arguments after the previous judges were unable to deliver a judgment before their retirement.

articles.headline: Shivakumar asks ECI to extend window for voter roll claims
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has requested the Election Commission of India to extend the deadline for filing claims and objections to the electoral rolls. He noted that over 10.8 million names were recently added to the draft rolls, and citizens need more time to verify their details. Shivakumar emphasized that the current window is insufficient for a thorough review.

articles.headline: CID takes over investigation into Hanur forest killings
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has handed over the investigation into the killing of three alleged poachers in the Hanur forest range to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). The deaths occurred during an encounter with forest personnel on August 14. The move follows demands for a transparent probe after post-mortem reports suggested the victims were shot from close range.

articles.headline: Karnataka to start cloud seeding to address rain deficit
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has decided to initiate cloud seeding operations in the Malnad and North Karnataka regions due to a significant rainfall deficit. Agriculture Minister N. Cheluvarayaswamy stated that the project aims to mitigate the impact of the dry spell on crops. The operations will begin after a technical committee completes the necessary evaluations and selects target areas.

articles.headline: CWMA maintains order for Cauvery water release to Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: The Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) has upheld its direction to Karnataka to release 9,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. The decision was made during the 56th meeting of the CWMA, which reviewed the water storage levels in the reservoirs. Karnataka had sought a reduction in the release due to low inflow, but the authority upheld the previous recommendation.

articles.headline: Governor suspends KPSC chairman over recruitment irregularities
articles.summary: Karnataka Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot has ordered the immediate suspension of the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar. The action follows allegations of corruption and procedural lapses in the selection of Gazetted Probationers. The state cabinet had recommended the suspension after an inquiry found evidence of malpractice in the recruitment process.

articles.headline: TVK and opposition clash over Parandur airport project clearance
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu's new political party TVK, led by actor Vijay, has joined the opposition in criticizing the state government's environmental clearance for the Parandur airport project. Critics argue that the project will destroy water bodies and agricultural land. The state government defended the move, stating the project is essential for industrial growth and that landowners will be compensated.

articles.headline: Telangana government defends prohibited list for private properties
articles.summary: The Telangana government has defended its decision to place thousands of private properties on a prohibited list under Section 22A of the Registration Act. Officials stated the move is necessary to prevent the illegal sale of government and Waqf lands. However, opposition parties and property owners have criticized the lack of transparency, claiming it has stalled legitimate transactions.

articles.headline: Jagan Mohan Reddy urges YSRCP workers to fight local polls
articles.summary: Former Andhra Pradesh CM Jagan Mohan Reddy has called on YSRCP workers to prepare for the upcoming local body elections with renewed aggression. Addressing a party meeting, he expressed confidence that the public remains supportive of the party despite the recent assembly election defeat. He urged cadre to highlight the shortcomings of the current NDA government in the state.

articles.headline: Five family members found dead in Srisailam lodge
articles.summary: The bodies of five family members, including three women and a teenager, were discovered in a lodge in the temple town of Srisailam, Andhra Pradesh. Preliminary police investigations suggest a mass suicide due to financial difficulties. The family had traveled from Chittoor and were found after lodge staff noticed a foul smell and alerted the authorities.

articles.headline: Kerala to promote Ayurveda and adventure tourism for Onam
articles.summary: Kerala Tourism Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas announced plans to attract more travelers during the Onam season by focusing on Ayurveda and adventure tourism. The department is launching new circuits that combine traditional wellness treatments with mountain trekking and water sports. The initiative aims to diversify the state's tourism offerings beyond backwaters and cultural festivals.

articles.headline: SC seeks Lok Sabha Speaker's reply on TMC disqualification plea
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has asked Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to respond to a petition filed by the Trinamool Congress (TMC) regarding the disqualification of MP Abhishek Banerjee. The TMC alleges that Banerjee’s suspension was done without following due process under the anti-defection law. The court will examine if the Speaker's delay in deciding on the disqualification is constitutionally valid.

articles.headline: Government relaxes sugar import norms to stabilize retail prices
articles.summary: The Union government has relaxed import norms for raw sugar to control rising retail prices in the domestic market. Importers are now allowed to refine and sell sugar within two months of the date of filing the bill of entry, an extension from the previous 45-day limit. This move is intended to increase the availability of sugar during the upcoming festival season and curb inflation.

articles.headline: SC directs Tarun Tejpal to surrender within three weeks
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal to surrender before the trial court within three weeks. The court rejected his plea for an extension of his bail, which was granted following his 2013 arrest in a sexual assault case. Tejpal is required to surrender before he can pursue further legal remedies against his conviction and 10-year prison sentence.

articles.headline: CBI registered record 1,005 cases in 2025: Annual report
articles.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered a record 1,005 cases and preliminary inquiries in 2025, according to its latest annual report. This marks a significant increase from previous years, which officials attributed to a proactive approach in investigating bank frauds and corruption. The report also highlights a higher conviction rate in cases related to economic offenses.

articles.headline: US sanctions four Indian firms for importing Iranian oil
articles.summary: The US Treasury Department has imposed sanctions on four India-based companies for their alleged involvement in the purchase and transport of Iranian petroleum products. The firms are accused of facilitating shipments worth millions of dollars in violation of US sanctions. This move is part of the US's broader strategy to cut off Iran's oil revenue and pressure the regime over its nuclear program.

articles.headline: Praggnanandhaa sets up Chess World Tour final against Caruana
articles.summary: Indian Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa defeated Germany's Vincent Keymer to reach the final of the Chess World Tour. He will face world number two Fabiano Caruana in the summit clash. The 21-year-old Indian displayed exceptional tactical skill throughout the tournament, securing his place as a top contender for the global title in classical and rapid formats.

articles.headline: Persisting retail F&O losses spur call for tighter eligibility filters
articles.summary: SEBI is considering stricter entry norms like income thresholds for retail traders in the derivatives segment to curb excessive speculative losses. Data shows nearly 97% of retail traders lost money in F&O contracts ending FY24, with average losses rising to ₹1.16 lakh. Market participants suggest suitability checks and product-level restrictions are needed to protect investors.

articles.headline: Overseas remittances surged 20% in June, led by travel and investments
articles.summary: India's outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) rose 20% year-on-year to $2.8 billion in June. Travel remained the dominant reason for spending, accounting for $1.37 billion. Investments in equity and debt reached an all-time high of $457 million, while deposits saw a sequential fall following a previous spike.

articles.headline: Centre mulls 100% mandatory random dope testing for airline pilots
articles.summary: The Civil Aviation Ministry is considering expanding mandatory random drug testing for pilots from 10% to 100%. Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu stated that the DGCA is assessing the feasibility of testing all 25,000 commercial pilots to ensure safety. Currently, India has over 11,000 active pilots. The proposal follows recent safety concerns in the industry.

articles.headline: US targets four Indian companies for alleged Iran oil links
articles.summary: The US Treasury has sanctioned four India-based companies—Portease Shipping, Safiran Shipping, Rising Gulf, and Prabhat Shipping—for alleged involvement in transporting Iranian petroleum products. The move is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' intended to pressure Tehran. Indian officials are monitoring the impact as the US expands its global enforcement of sanctions.

articles.headline: ₹1,755-crore tax demand notice against Tata Steel stayed by Authority
articles.summary: In a relief for Tata Steel, the Revisional Authority has stayed a ₹1,755-crore demand notice issued by a Jharkhand district office. The notice was related to alleged excess extraction of iron ore from the West Bokaro Colliery between FY01 and FY07. The stay remains in place pending the final disposal of the company's revision application.

articles.headline: Suzlon opens wind energy projects worth ₹10,500 crore in Andhra
articles.summary: Suzlon Group has inaugurated 1,325 MW of wind energy projects in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh, with an investment of ₹10,500 crore. The projects are expected to generate 1,600 jobs. Minister Nara Lokesh also opened Suzlon’s blade manufacturing unit, highlighting the state's focus on green energy and industrial expansion.

articles.headline: No clarity yet on Federal Bank and Jana SFB deal
articles.summary: Federal Bank has clarified it is evaluating various growth opportunities but denied any definitive deal to acquire a stake in Jana Small Finance Bank. Reports had suggested Blackstone might invest ₹1,696 crore to acquire a 9.99% stake in Federal Bank to fund such an acquisition. Federal Bank shares ended slightly lower on the stock exchanges following the news.

articles.headline: Va Tech Wabag makes Kuwait debut with desalination plant project
articles.summary: Water technology firm Va Tech Wabag has secured a contract for the Doha SWRO Desalination Plant with Re-carbonation Stage-II in Kuwait. This marks the company's first major order in the country. The project, awarded by the Ministry of Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy, involves a five-year operation and maintenance period following construction.

articles.headline: Mondelez, Amway take corrective action after FSSAI labelling notices
articles.summary: Following a crackdown on misleading claims, major food companies like Mondelez India and Amway have corrected labels and withdrawn advertisements. FSSAI flagged issues related to 'energy' and 'protein' claims on products like Bournvita and Nutrilite. Most companies have complied by removing misleading tags from packaging and promotional materials.

articles.headline: L&T’s West Asia order book swells with ₹50,000-crore August wins
articles.summary: Larsen & Toubro has secured massive orders in West Asia, with contract wins exceeding ₹50,000 crore in August alone. The latest project involves three battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in Saudi Arabia worth between ₹5,000-10,000 crore. West Asia now contributes over a third of the company's total EPC pipeline as renewable energy demand grows.

articles.headline: IPO-bound ESDS flags local protest impact on data centre biz
articles.summary: Data centre provider ESDS Software Solutions has highlighted local protests against new facilities as a significant business risk in its IPO filings. Residents in areas like Navi Mumbai have protested against potential environmental impacts and resource consumption of large data hubs. The company plans to raise ₹600-800 crore via an upcoming public issue.

articles.headline: CNH to invest ₹1,000 crore to double India tractor output
articles.summary: US-based CNH Industrial plans to invest ₹1,000 crore to double its tractor manufacturing capacity in India by 2030. The company aims to increase annual production from 48,000 to 70,000 units. A significant portion of this investment will go towards R&D and expanding its facility in Greater Noida to serve both domestic and export markets like Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.

articles.headline: India current account balance holds firm despite flaring trade gap
articles.summary: India's current account deficit (CAD) remained stable at $3.1 billion in Q1 FY27, according to RBI data. While the merchandise trade gap widened due to higher imports, it was offset by strong services exports and steady secondary income. Net foreign direct investment inflows also improved to $7.8 billion during the April-June quarter.

articles.headline: Samudra Manthan scheme: Govt prepares roadmap for oil drilling
articles.summary: The Ministry of Petroleum is finalising an $8.8-billion roadmap for drilling, seismic surveys, and rig deployment under the Samudra Manthan scheme. The project aims to boost domestic oil and gas production in deep and ultra-deep waters of the Andaman, Cauvery, and Mahanadi basins. ONGC and Oil India will lead the exploration efforts with government fiscal support.

articles.headline: Indian refiners lean on Russia and UAE for August imports
articles.summary: Indian refiners are increasing crude oil imports from Russia, the UAE, and South America in August due to persistent shipping disruptions in the Red Sea. Russia remains India's largest supplier, followed by the UAE and Brazil. Experts noted that refining Russian crude remains economically feasible despite sanctions and volatile global price differentials.

articles.headline: Jaishankar calls for urgent steps to address India-Russia trade deficit
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has urged Russia to address the growing trade imbalance, with India's deficit reaching nearly $60 billion. During talks in Moscow, he called for removing non-tariff barriers and improving market access for Indian products in sectors like energy and technology. Both nations aim to reach a $100-billion bilateral trade target by 2030.

articles.headline: Unkind cut: Bank levy on cash withdrawals at ATMs is unfair
articles.summary: State Bank of India's decision to charge even basic savings account (BSBDA) holders for ATM withdrawals beyond a monthly limit has drawn criticism. Critics argue these levies punish low-income groups who rely on cash for daily livelihoods. While the move aims to promote digital payments, it disproportionately affects those with limited digital literacy or access.

articles.headline: Repowering Tamil Nadu’s wind power sector to regain first-mover advantage
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu needs to urgently modernize its aging wind turbines to increase power generation efficiency. Many turbines installed in the 1990s produce far less power than modern equivalents. Policy experts suggest streamlining the repowering process through better grid infrastructure, single-window clearances, and dedicated financial models for small and mid-sized farmers.

articles.headline: The art of no deal: Lessons from US-India trade pact talks
articles.summary: A proposed US-India trade pact remains elusive as both nations navigate complex regulatory and economic priorities. While Washington seeks greater market access for agricultural and medical products, New Delhi is wary of impacts on local industry and digital sovereignty. Recent diplomatic engagements suggest progress on some technical levels, but a broad trade deal is not imminent.

articles.headline: Nifty surges 115 points as F&O expiry day swings conclude
articles.summary: The Nifty 50 rose 115.50 points to end at 24,334, while the BSE Sensex gained 286 points. The market saw a late recovery as crude oil prices fell and a short-covering rally emerged during the monthly F&O expiry. Sectorally, healthcare, consumer durables, and pharmaceuticals were top performers, while PSU banks and energy stocks faced some pressure.

articles.headline: SEBI slaps ₹33-crore fine on Vardhaman Cloud for IPO fund diversion
articles.summary: SEBI has fined Vardhaman Cloud Ltd and its promoters ₹33.08 crore for misrepresenting company financials and diverting ₹128.77 crore of IPO proceeds. The regulator found that funds meant for business expansion were siphoned off through various entities. The involved individuals have been barred from the securities market for up to seven years.

articles.headline: Rays of Relief social firm to launch ₹125-crore IPO
articles.summary: Rays of Relief, a for-profit social enterprise focusing on neurodevelopmental disorders, plans to raise ₹125 crore through an initial public offering. The firm provides therapy for conditions like autism and cerebral palsy. Proceeds will be used to expand its network from current major cities to tier-1 and tier-2 locations across India by FY29.

articles.headline: RBI Bulletin: Economy displays strength despite global headwinds
articles.summary: The RBI's August bulletin states the Indian economy remains resilient, supported by robust manufacturing and services activity. While global geopolitical tensions and high food prices pose risks, domestic demand remains buoyant. The report notes that headline inflation eased slightly in July, though some supply-side pressures on food items like pulses and oils persist.

articles.headline: NRI deposit inflows up 22% to $2.8 billion in April-June
articles.summary: Inflows into non-resident Indian (NRI) deposits surged 22% year-on-year to $2.8 billion during the first quarter of FY27. Total outstanding NRI deposits stood at $169 billion as of June. The growth was primarily driven by higher interest rates offered by Indian banks and stable rupee-dollar dynamics, making local deposits more attractive to the diaspora.

articles.headline: Flow of financial resources to commercial sector hits ₹10.65 lakh cr
articles.summary: Total financial resources flowing to the commercial sector reached ₹10.65 lakh crore in the first four months of the current fiscal year, up from ₹4.48 lakh crore last year. Bank credit grew by ₹7.01 lakh crore, while non-bank sources like IPOs and bond issuances also saw significant activity. This indicates strong demand for capital across various industrial sectors.

articles.headline: Public sector banks more efficient than private lenders, says paper
articles.summary: A working paper by the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister suggests that public sector banks (PSBs) have become more efficient than many private and foreign banks. The report uses efficiency scores based on data from FY15 to FY26, noting that PSBs showed significant improvement following recapitalization and technological upgrades.

articles.headline: TN govt defends Parandur airport decision and seeks alternative sites
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government defended its choice of Parandur for Chennai's second airport, citing it as the most suitable location among those studied. However, the state is also identifying alternative sites for greenfield airports in other regions. To address local concerns, the government has decided against an earlier plan to acquire 2,000 acres of agricultural land.

articles.headline: GST notice must contain clear grounds for fraud or suppression: SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that GST show-cause notices must specifically state grounds for 'fraud' or 'wilful misstatement' rather than using vague terms. The court noted that a lack of clear facts in a notice prevents taxpayers from filing proper responses. This judgment is expected to bring greater clarity and accountability to tax assessment procedures.

articles.headline: Avaada in deal to develop zero-carbon green industrial campus
articles.summary: Avaada Group has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Haryana government to develop a 300-acre zero-carbon green industrial campus. The ₹10,000-crore project is expected to create 5,000 jobs and provide renewable energy infrastructure for industries. The initiative aligns with Haryana’s goals to promote sustainable manufacturing and clean energy tech.

articles.headline: C-DOT to drive India’s shift toward global telecom leadership
articles.summary: Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia stated that C-DOT is crucial for India's transition from self-reliance to global leadership in 4G and 5G technology. Speaking at C-DOT's 43rd foundation day, he highlighted the development of an indigenous 4G stack and 14 new quantum products. The government aims to position India as a key exporter of high-tech telecom equipment.

articles.headline: Coking coal prices poised to be volatile in the short-term
articles.summary: Global coking coal prices are expected to remain volatile due to China's new mine regulations and fluctuations in steel production. While Indian demand for coking coal is rising, supply constraints from major exporters like Australia could keep prices high. Analysts expect prices to hover around $220-225 per tonne for the remainder of the year.

articles.headline: Shivraj Singh Chouhan asks ICAR to tackle onion price gap
articles.summary: Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has urged the Indian Council of Agricultural Research to find ways to reduce the wide gap between farm-gate and retail onion prices. He noted that while farmers often get low prices, consumers pay significantly more. The government has started selling onions at a subsidized rate of ₹35 per kg in major cities to provide relief.

articles.headline: Centre set to ban highly hazardous pesticide Carbosulfan
articles.summary: The Union government has proposed a ban on Carbosulfan, a pesticide used primarily in rice, cotton, and vegetables, due to its high toxicity to humans and animals. Following recommendations from an expert committee, the Ministry of Agriculture will stop its manufacture and sale. The decision follows reports of several pesticide-related deaths and environmental damage.

articles.headline: Defence Ministry plans to fast-track licensing to under three weeks
articles.summary: The Ministry of Defence has created a concept paper aimed at reducing the processing time for private sector manufacturing licenses to less than three weeks. Currently, licensing can take much longer due to multi-agency clearances. The new portal and streamlined procedures are intended to boost domestic defence production and simplify ease of doing business for SMEs.

articles.headline: India targets rise in air cargo handling to 10 mt by 2030
articles.summary: Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu announced a target to increase India's air cargo handling capacity to 10 million tonnes by 2030, up from the current 3.96 million tonnes. The government plans to develop integrated air cargo hubs and improve transshipment efficiency to turn India into a global logistics backbone. The focus will be on digital processing and infrastructure expansion.

articles.headline: Govt launches reference standards to detect carcinogenic impurities in drugs
articles.summary: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission has launched seven new reference standards to help pharmaceutical companies detect nitrosamine impurities, which can be carcinogenic. These standards will help ensure the safety of drugs used for conditions like hypertension and gastric disorders. The move aims to align Indian drug manufacturing with international quality and safety benchmarks.

articles.headline: Mumbai airport asks airlines to shift 30% of international flights
articles.summary: The Adani-run Mumbai International Airport has asked airlines to move 30% of their international operations from Terminal 2 to the upcoming Navi Mumbai International Airport by 2027. This move is intended to decongest the existing airport, which currently handles nearly 50 million passengers annually. Major carriers like IndiGo and Air India have been briefed on the plan.

articles.headline: Almost half of global oil flows now from risk zones
articles.summary: Nearly half of the world's daily oil supply is currently under threat from production and refining capacity outages due to geopolitical conflicts and extreme weather. Supply shocks have now eclipsed previous energy crises, with significant disruptions reported in Russia, Libya, and the Red Sea, impacting global energy security and driving higher fuel prices.

articles.headline: Canada retaliates against US with tariffs up to 50 percent
articles.summary: Canada has announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on US imports following President Trump's threat to rename Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' and cut off electricity exports. The escalating trade war involves products ranging from steel and nickel to dairy and cosmetic goods, totaling a C$7.5 billion response to the latest US tariff measures.

articles.headline: Oman and Iran plan temporary shipping lane via Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran and Oman are discussing the establishment of a temporary corridor through the Strait of Hormuz to ensure the safe passage of maritime trade. The initiative follows recent attacks on tankers and heightened regional tensions. Both nations aim to regulate transit and maintain stability in the vital waterway despite ongoing international sanctions.

articles.headline: India remains Canada's top source for permanent residents in 2026
articles.summary: Official data reveals that India remains the primary source of permanent residents for Canada. In the first half of 2026, 44,335 Indians were admitted, making up 24.6% of the total intake. While numbers have dipped slightly from previous peaks, India continues to lead, followed by the Philippines and China, amidst Canada's evolving immigration levels.

articles.headline: FDA raids flag poor hygiene at Bengaluru's elite club kitchens
articles.summary: The Food and Drugs Administration conducted raids at several elite clubs in Bengaluru, uncovering significant lapses in food safety and hygiene. Inspectors found poor storage, lack of mandatory labeling, and improper waste management. Establishments have been given 15 days to address these violations or face further legal action under the Food Safety Act.

articles.headline: Karnataka plans Rs 27 crore cloud seeding amid rainfall deficit
articles.summary: Facing a 31% rainfall deficit this monsoon, the Karnataka government has approved a Rs 27 crore cloud seeding operation. The project will target four river divisions over 60 days to mitigate the water crisis and support parched agricultural regions. The state is also set to release 9,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu as per CWRC directives.

articles.headline: Ahmedabad-Mumbai bullet train project cost doubles to Rs 2.1 lakh crore
articles.summary: The estimated cost of the 508 km Ahmedabad-Mumbai high-speed rail project has nearly doubled to Rs 2.1 lakh crore from the initial Rs 1.1 lakh crore. Significant land acquisition delays and rising infrastructure costs are the primary reasons for the increase. The first phase of the corridor is now expected to be operational by August 2027.

articles.headline: India and China hold talks to stabilize border peace
articles.summary: In the latest round of Special Representatives Dialogue, India and China endorsed ongoing efforts to formalize border peace and maintain stability along the Line of Actual Control. Both nations emphasized the importance of tranquility for the broader bilateral relationship, working toward a sustainable and predictable framework for border management.

articles.headline: Teenager Vandan Alankar beats Magnus Carlsen in chess tournament
articles.summary: 15-year-old Vandan Alankar shocked the chess world by defeating world number one Magnus Carlsen in just 50 moves during an online tournament. His parents only discovered the feat when he went to bed shortly after. Alankar had earlier won three other games in the tournament, demonstrating remarkable focus and skill against the former world champion.

articles.headline: Poisonous Datura fruit delivered as 'free gift' lands woman in hospital
articles.summary: A woman in Bengaluru was hospitalized after consuming a toxic Datura fruit that was delivered as a 'free fruit' item by a grocery app. The app had erroneously listed the poisonous plant, which can cause hallucinations and cardiac issues, as a consumable item. Health authorities have since cracked down on the platform for failing to verify food safety.

articles.headline: Karnataka to resume student union elections in colleges after years
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has announced the resumption of student union elections in all pre-university and degree colleges from the current academic year. The move ends a long-standing ban and aims to foster leadership skills among the youth. However, candidates must be at the first level and unaffiliated with any political parties to be eligible.

articles.headline: Retired techie's speeding car kills hair stylist in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A 33-year-old hair stylist was killed on Bengaluru's Kaggadasapura Main Road after being struck by a speeding car driven by a 63-year-old retired techie. CCTV footage revealed the car was traveling at high speed, and the driver reportedly mistook the accelerator for the brake. The driver has been booked for causing death by negligence.

articles.headline: Study links Bengaluru's air pollution to increasing hair fall
articles.summary: A new clinical study suggests a strong link between Bengaluru's high air pollution levels and sudden hair loss conditions like alopecia areata. Researchers found that tiny particles from dust and vehicle smoke penetrate the scalp, triggering inflammation and oxidative stress that damage hair follicles. Doctors advise minimized exposure and regular scalp care.

articles.headline: Indian undergraduate applications to US universities drop by 15 percent
articles.summary: For the 2025-26 academic cycle, undergraduate applications from India to US universities have declined by 15% after a decade of steady growth. Analysts attribute the drop to rising costs, visa complexities, and a shift toward domestic alternatives. Conversely, applications from China saw a 15% increase, reversing their previous downward trend.

articles.headline: Goa to introduce stringent law against unlawful religious conversions
articles.summary: The Goa government is set to introduce a strict anti-conversion law that prescribes jail terms of up to 14 years and heavy fines for offenders. The proposed law targets conversions through force, allurement, or misrepresentation. It also makes it mandatory for individuals to provide a two-month notice to authorities before changing their religion.

articles.headline: Lasalgaon onion prices drop to 4,000 rupees per quintal
articles.summary: Wholesale onion prices at Asia's largest market in Lasalgaon have fallen to Rs 4,000 per quintal from earlier highs. The price drop is linked to increased arrivals and the central government's efforts to release buffer stocks in major cities. This move aims to provide relief to retail consumers who have faced rising costs in recent months.

articles.headline: RBI flags persistent price risks for second time in August
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has issued its second warning this month regarding persistent inflation risks. High food prices and volatile global energy costs are major concerns that could impact economic growth. While domestic demand remains strong, the RBI stressed that maintaining price stability is critical for long-term financial health.

articles.headline: Saraswati idol found in Madhya Pradesh reveals ancient musical heritage
articles.summary: Archaeologists have discovered an 1,800-year-old idol of the goddess Saraswati in Madhya Pradesh. The artifact, which depicts the goddess holding a harp-like instrument, provides significant evidence of India's rich musical tradition during the 2nd century AD. The discovery is hailed as a vital piece of national cultural heritage.

articles.headline: Anaya Bangar returns to competitive cricket following gender-affirming surgery
articles.summary: Anaya Bangar, daughter of former India cricketer Sanjay Bangar, is set to return to competitive cricket in Australia. Cricket Australia has confirmed her eligibility to play in women's cricket from March 2027. Bangar expressed deep gratitude for the opportunity to play the sport she loves again, highlighting the importance of inclusion in sports.

articles.headline: Foreign investors pump Rs 25,000 crore into Indian equities
articles.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) bought Indian equities worth over Rs 25,000 crore in August, marking a 23-month high. The surge in investment is driven by stable macroeconomic indicators and strong corporate earnings. This inflow has helped the benchmark Nifty 50 and Sensex reach new heights, reflecting global confidence in the resilience of the Indian economy despite global volatility.

articles.headline: ICMR reports 98% of seasonal flu cases are H1N1
articles.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) reported that 98% of influenza cases tested this season belong to the H1N1 subtype. While there is a rise in cases, the ICMR stated there is no reason for panic as no deaths have been reported from this subtype so far. Health officials have advised schools and parents to follow preventive measures as seasonal cases typically peak in August.

articles.headline: OpenAI chips Jalapeno show performance edge over Nvidia in tests
articles.summary: OpenAI’s new Jalapeno chips reportedly outperformed Nvidia's current lineup in preliminary tests for AI model inference. The chips, developed with Broadcom, showed superior speed in processing AI prompts. While Nvidia remains dominant in training chips, OpenAI’s hardware push aims to reduce reliance on external suppliers and cut long-term costs for its AI infrastructure.

articles.headline: DGCA considers mandatory annual random drug tests for all pilots
articles.summary: India's aviation regulator, the DGCA, is weighing a policy to conduct annual random drug tests on all 25,000 commercial pilots. Current rules require testing at least 10% of flight crews annually. The proposed world-first move aims to ensure total safety and sobriety in the cockpit. Pilot unions have expressed concerns over existing infrastructure to handle such massive testing volumes.

articles.headline: Supreme Court refuses to widen remit of July 20 probe
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday declined a plea to expand the scope of a high-powered inquiry committee investigating the July 20 violence in Delhi. A bench led by Justice R Subhash Reddy stated it would conduct its own independent probe into allegations of excessive police force. The court dismissed petitions seeking to include the role of senior government officials in the investigation.

articles.headline: NSA Ajit Doval stresses border peace in China talks
articles.summary: Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing for the 25th round of boundary talks. Doval emphasized that peace and tranquility along the border are essential for overall bilateral ties. Both sides discussed a framework for resolving the 3,488km border dispute and agreed to maintain progress on boundary delimitation and stability.

articles.headline: Country music icon Dolly Parton dies at age 80
articles.summary: Dolly Parton, the legendary American singer-songwriter and humanitarian, has passed away at the age of 80. Known for hits like 'Jolene' and 'I Will Always Love You,' Parton sold over 100 million records and won 11 Grammy awards. Her career spanned decades, during which she became a symbol of resilience and cross-generational appeal in country and pop music.

articles.headline: Court allows accused in Renukaswamy murder case to turn approver
articles.summary: A Bengaluru court has allowed Pradosh S., one of the accused in the Renukaswamy murder case, to turn approver. The court granted the petition after the prosecution stated that Pradosh’s testimony would provide crucial evidence against other accused, including actor Darshan. Pradosh will now be treated as a witness on the condition that he provides a full and truthful disclosure of the crime.

articles.headline: Modi reviews six major infrastructure projects across nine states
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi reviewed the progress of six key infrastructure projects with a combined cost of over Rs 30,000 crore. These projects span across nine states and include critical rail and road corridors. Modi emphasized the need for timely completion and directed state governments to resolve land acquisition and utility-shifting issues to avoid further delays.

articles.headline: Private industry granted access to DRDO missile technology
articles.summary: In a major boost for the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' initiative, the Ministry of Defence has allowed private industries to access DRDO-developed missile technologies. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said this transfer of technology (ToT) would enable Indian firms to manufacture advanced conventional missile systems. The move is expected to enhance domestic production and increase India's defense exports.

articles.headline: CIA chief visits Moscow for talks on Ukraine and Iran
articles.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a rare visit to Moscow to discuss the ongoing wars in Ukraine and Iran with Russian intelligence counterparts. The talks reportedly focused on de-escalation strategies and the role of third-party mediation. While details remain sparse, the visit signifies an attempt to maintain communication channels between Washington and Moscow amid high global tensions.

articles.headline: Air India seeks $1.5 billion funding from Tata and SIA
articles.summary: Air India has requested an additional $1.5 billion in fresh equity from its owners, the Tata Group and Singapore Airlines (SIA). The funds are required to support the airline's fleet expansion and to cover operational losses as it undergoes a massive transformation. The airline plans to induct over 50 new aircraft in the next year to bolster its domestic and international network.

articles.headline: India takes command in first Test against Sri Lanka
articles.summary: The Indian cricket team established a dominant position on Day 3 of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Mumbai. After being bowled out for 467, India's bowlers, led by Prasidh Krishna, reduced Sri Lanka to 220/7 by stumps. Sri Lanka still trails by 247 runs and faces a daunting task to avoid a follow-on, with India firmly in control of the match's progression.
